questions.text: जल का विद्युत-अपघटन एक वियोजन (अपघटन) अभिक्रिया है। जल के विद्युत-अपघटन के समय इलेक्ट्रोडों पर मुक्त गैसों – हाइड्रोजन और ऑक्सीजन के द्रव्यमानों का अनुपात (MH : MO) होता है:
questions.text_english: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mass ratio (MH : MO) of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes during electrolysis of water is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 1 : 8. During electrolysis of water (2H2O → 2H2 + O2), 4 g of hydrogen (2 moles) and 32 g of oxygen (1 mole) are produced. Thus the mass ratio MH : MO = 4 : 32 = 1 : 8. Options A and B are incorrect because they do not reflect actual molar masses; option C (1:2) represents the mole ratio of H2 to O2, not the mass ratio.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 1 : 8 है। जल के विद्युत-अपघटन में (2H2O → 2H2 + O2), 4 g हाइड्रोजन और 32 g ऑक्सीजन उत्पन्न होती है। अतः द्रव्यमान अनुपात MH : MO = 4 : 32 = 1 : 8।
questions.topic: Electrolysis of water / Decomposition reaction

questions.text: वायु की उपस्थिति में ऐलुमिनियम और मैग्नीशियम के दहन होने पर बनने वाले उत्पाद क्रमशः हैं:
questions.text_english: The products formed when Aluminium and Magnesium are burnt in the presence of air respectively are:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Al2O3 and MgO. When aluminium burns in air, it reacts with oxygen to form aluminium oxide: 4Al + 3O2 → 2Al2O3. When magnesium burns in air, it forms magnesium oxide: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. Al has a valency of +3 and O has -2, giving Al2O3; Mg has a valency of +2 and O has -2, giving MgO. All other options have incorrect chemical formulae.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) Al2O3 और MgO है। ऐलुमिनियम दहन पर Al2O3 और मैग्नीशियम दहन पर MgO बनाता है।
questions.topic: Combustion of metals / Oxides of metals

questions.text: निम्नलिखित तालिका में pH पैमाने पर चार विलयनों A, B, C और D के pH मान दर्शाए गए हैं: (pH scale: A~4, B~7, C~11, D~14) ये चारों विलयन A, B, C और D क्रमशः हैं
questions.text_english: The following table shows the pH values of four solutions A, B, C and D on a pH scale. (A~4, B~7, C~11, D~14) The solutions A, B, C and D respectively are of a

options.A: Strong acid, weak acid, neutral, strong base
options.B: Weak acid, neutral, weak base, strong base
options.C: Weak acid, neutral, strong base, weak base
options.D: Weak acid, neutral, strong base, strong acid

options_english.A: Strong acid, weak acid, neutral, strong base
options_english.B: Weak acid, neutral, weak base, strong base
options_english.C: Weak acid, neutral, strong base, weak base
options_english.D: Weak acid, neutral, strong base, strong acid

questions.image_description: A pH scale from 1 to 14 with four markers: A placed around pH 4 (acidic), B placed at pH 7 (neutral), C placed around pH 11 (alkaline), and D placed at pH 14 (strongly alkaline).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Weak acid, neutral, weak base, strong base. Solution A has pH around 4, which is mildly acidic — hence a weak acid. Solution B has pH 7 — neutral. Solution C has pH around 11 — moderately alkaline, hence a weak base. Solution D has pH 14 — strongly alkaline, hence a strong base. Option A is incorrect because pH 4 does not indicate a strong acid (strong acids have pH close to 1).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। A (pH~4) दुर्बल अम्ल, B (pH 7) उदासीन, C (pH~11) दुर्बल क्षारक और D (pH~14) प्रबल क्षारक है।
questions.topic: pH scale / Strength of acids and bases

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं पर विचार कीजिए:
(i) तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल, सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड से अभिक्रिया करता है।
(ii) मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड, तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल से अभिक्रिया करता है।
(iii) कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड, सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड से अभिक्रिया करती है।
यह पाया जाता है कि प्रत्येक प्रकरण में:
questions.text_english:
Consider the following reactions:
(i) Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide.
(ii) Magnesium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid.
(iii) Carbon dioxide reacts with sodium hydroxide.
It is found that in each case:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Salt and water is formed. In reaction (i), HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O (neutralisation). In reaction (ii), MgO + 2HCl → MgCl2 + H2O (base–acid reaction). In reaction (iii), CO2 + 2NaOH → Na2CO3 + H2O (acidic oxide with base). In all three cases, a salt and water are formed. Option B is wrong because Na2CO3 is a basic salt, not neutral. Option C is wrong as no hydrogen gas is produced in any of these reactions.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। तीनों अभिक्रियाओं में लवण और जल बनता है।
questions.topic: Neutralisation reactions / Reactions of acids and bases

questions.text: दो तत्त्वों A और B के बीच अभिक्रिया से कोई यौगिक C बनता है। A इलेक्ट्रॉन खोता है तथा B इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करता है। यौगिक C निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक गुण नहीं दर्शाएगा?
questions.text_english: Reaction between two elements A and B, forms a compound C. A loses electrons and B gains electrons. Which one of the following properties will not be shown by compound C?

options.B: It is highly soluble in water.
options.C: It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.
options.D: It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.

options_english.B: It is highly soluble in water.
options_english.C: It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.
options_english.D: It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Compound C is an ionic compound because A loses electrons and B gains them, forming oppositely charged ions. Ionic compounds are characterised by strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions — not weak forces. Hence, option C is the property that ionic compounds do NOT show. Options A, B, and D are all genuine properties of ionic compounds: they have high melting points, are generally soluble in water, and conduct electricity in molten or dissolved states.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। यौगिक C आयनिक यौगिक है जिसमें विपरीत आवेशित आयनों के बीच प्रबल स्थिर-विद्युत आकर्षण बल होता है, न कि दुर्बल। अतः (C) वह गुण है जो यह यौगिक नहीं दर्शाएगा।
questions.topic: Ionic bonding / Properties of ionic compounds

questions.text: विद्युत-अपघटनी अपचयन प्रक्रिया द्वारा गलित क्लोराइडों से प्राप्त होने वाली धातुएँ हैं:
questions.text_english: The metals obtained from their molten chlorides by the process of electrolytic reduction are:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Calcium and magnesium. Metals that are very high in the reactivity series, such as calcium, magnesium, sodium, aluminium, etc., cannot be extracted by reduction with carbon; they require electrolytic reduction of their molten chlorides. Gold and silver are low in the reactivity series and are found free in nature. Iron is extracted by reduction with coke (carbon). Sodium is also extracted by electrolysis, but it is not paired with iron. Calcium and magnesium are both extracted by electrolytic reduction of their molten chlorides (CaCl2 and MgCl2 respectively).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) कैल्शियम और मैग्नीशियम है। ये सक्रियता श्रेणी में ऊपर स्थित धातुएँ हैं जिन्हें गलित क्लोराइडों के विद्युत-अपघटनी अपचयन द्वारा प्राप्त किया जाता है।
questions.topic: Extraction of metals / Electrolytic reduction

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए किस विकल्प में मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड बनना सही दिखाया गया है?
questions.text_english: The formation of magnesium oxide is correctly shown in option:

options.A: Mg transfers 2 electrons to O, forming Mg2+ and [O]2-
options.B: Mg transfers 1 electron to O, forming Mg+ and [O]-
options.C: Mg transfers 2 electrons to two O atoms, forming Mg2+ and [O-]2
options.D: 2Mg each transfers 1 electron to O2, forming [Mg2+]2 [O2-]

options_english.A: Mg transfers 2 electrons to O, forming Mg2+ and [O]2-
options_english.B: Mg transfers 1 electron to O, forming Mg+ and [O]-
options_english.C: Mg transfers 2 electrons to two O atoms, forming Mg2+ and [O-]2
options_english.D: 2Mg each transfers 1 electron to O2, forming [Mg2+]2 [O2-]

questions.image_description: Four electron dot diagrams showing different ways magnesium reacts with oxygen. Option A shows Mg losing 2 electrons to one O atom to form Mg2+ and O2-. Option B shows Mg losing 1 electron to form Mg+ and O-. Option C shows Mg losing 2 electrons shared between two O atoms. Option D shows two Mg atoms each losing 1 electron to O2.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Magnesium (electronic configuration 2,8,2) loses 2 electrons from its outermost shell to form Mg2+. Oxygen (electronic configuration 2,6) gains 2 electrons to complete its octet and forms O2-. Therefore, one Mg atom reacts with one O atom and the formula of magnesium oxide is MgO. Option A correctly shows Mg donating 2 electrons to one O atom to form Mg2+ and O2-. Options B, C, and D show incorrect electron transfer (1 electron, split electrons, or wrong stoichiometry).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। Mg 2 इलेक्ट्रॉन खोकर Mg2+ बनाता है और O 2 इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण कर O2- बनाता है। अतः MgO बनता है।
questions.topic: Ionic bond formation / Electron dot structure of MgO

questions.text: मुँह में लार का कम मात्रा में स्रावित होना किस परिवर्तन को प्रभावित करता है?
questions.text_english: Secretion of less saliva in mouth will effect the conversion of:

options.B: fats into fatty acids and glycerol

options_english.B: fats into fatty acids and glycerol

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) starch into simple sugars. Saliva contains the enzyme salivary amylase (ptyalin), which begins the digestion of starch (a complex carbohydrate) into simpler sugars (maltose) in the mouth. If less saliva is secreted, this conversion will be affected. Protein digestion (option A) begins in the stomach by pepsin; fat digestion (option B) occurs in the small intestine by lipase; fermentation of sugar to alcohol (option D) is not a normal digestive process in humans.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। लार में लाइपेज एन्जाइम होता है जो स्टार्च का सरल शर्करा में पाचन करता है। लार कम होने पर यह परिवर्तन प्रभावित होगा।
questions.topic: Digestion / Role of saliva

questions.text: वह कौन-सा पादप हॉर्मोन है जिसकी सांद्रता, प्ररोह के प्रकाश से दूर वाले भाग की कोशिकाओं को लम्बाई में वृद्धि के लिए उद्दीपित करती है?
questions.text_english: The plant hormone whose concentration stimulates the cells to grow longer on the side of the shoot which is away from light is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Auxins. Auxins are plant hormones produced at the tip of the shoot. When light falls on a shoot from one side, auxins migrate to the shaded (dark) side. Their higher concentration on the dark side stimulates those cells to elongate more, causing the shoot to bend towards the light — a phenomenon called phototropism. Cytokinins promote cell division; gibberellins promote stem elongation and seed germination; adrenaline is an animal hormone, not a plant hormone.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) ऑक्सिन है। ऑक्सिन प्रकाश से दूर वाले भाग की कोशिकाओं को लम्बाई में वृद्धि के लिए उद्दीपित करता है, जिससे प्ररोह प्रकाश की ओर मुड़ता है।
questions.topic: Plant hormones / Phototropism / Auxins

questions.text:
उभयलिंगी पुष्प के विषय में सही कथन है/हैं:
(i) इनमें पुंकेसर और स्त्रीकेसर दोनों होते हैं।
(ii) इनमें या तो पुंकेसर होता है अथवा स्त्रीकेसर होता है।
(iii) ये या तो स्वपरागण दर्शाते हैं अथवा परपरागण दर्शाते हैं।
(iv) ये अपने आप फल उत्पन्न नहीं कर सकते हैं।
questions.text_english:
The correct/true statement(s) for a bisexual flower is/are:
(i) They possess both stamen and pistil.
(ii) They possess either stamen or pistil.
(iii) They exhibit either self-pollination or cross-pollination.
(iv) They cannot produce fruits on their own.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (i) and (iii). A bisexual (hermaphrodite) flower possesses both male (stamen) and female (pistil) reproductive organs — so statement (i) is correct. Because they have both stamens and pistils, bisexual flowers can undergo either self-pollination (pollen from the same flower) or cross-pollination (pollen from another flower) — so statement (iii) is correct. Statement (ii) is incorrect because unisexual flowers (not bisexual) have either stamen or pistil. Statement (iv) is incorrect because bisexual flowers can produce fruits on their own through self-pollination.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) (i) और (iii) है। उभयलिंगी पुष्प में पुंकेसर और स्त्रीकेसर दोनों होते हैं और ये स्वपरागण या परपरागण दोनों प्रदर्शित कर सकते हैं।
questions.topic: Bisexual flowers / Pollination

questions.text: गोल और हरे (RRyy) बीजों वाले मटर के पौधों का झुर्रीदार और पीले (rrYY) बीजों वाले मटर के पौधों के साथ संकरण कराया गया। F1 संतति के पौधों द्वारा विकसित बीज होंगे:
questions.text_english: If pea plants with round and green seeds (RRyy) are crossed with pea plants having wrinkled and yellow seeds (rrYY), the seeds developed by the plants of F1 generation will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 100% round and yellow. The parent genotypes are RRyy (round, green) and rrYY (wrinkled, yellow). The F1 generation will have the genotype RrYy. Since R (round) is dominant over r (wrinkled), and Y (yellow) is dominant over y (green), all F1 plants will display the dominant phenotype: round and yellow seeds. Therefore, 100% of F1 seeds will be round and yellow. A dihybrid ratio of 9:3:3:1 appears only in the F2 generation.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) 100% गोल और पीले है। F1 पीढ़ी में सभी पौधों का जीनोटाइप RrYy होगा, अतः सभी बीज गोल (R प्रभावी) और पीले (Y प्रभावी) होंगे।
questions.topic: Mendelian genetics / Dihybrid cross / Dominance

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित ग्लूकोज़ के विखण्डन का पथ दर्शाया गया है:
ग्लूकोज़ →(a)→ पायरुवेट + ऊर्जा →(b)→ लैक्टिक अम्ल + ऊर्जा
स्थल 'a' और 'b' क्रमशः हैं:
questions.text_english:
The breakdown of glucose has taken the following pathway:
Glucose →(a)→ Pyruvate + Energy →(b)→ Lactic acid + Energy
The sites 'a' and 'b' respectively are:

options.A: Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
options.B: Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells
options.D: Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells

options_english.A: Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
options_english.B: Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells
options_english.D: Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells. Glycolysis — the breakdown of glucose to pyruvate — occurs in the cytoplasm (site 'a') and does not require oxygen. Subsequently, when oxygen is absent (anaerobic conditions), pyruvate is converted to lactic acid in muscle cells (site 'b'). This happens during intense exercise when oxygen supply is insufficient. Yeast cells convert pyruvate to ethanol and CO2, not lactic acid. Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle), not glycolysis.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) कोशिकाद्रव्य और ऑक्सीजन के अभाव वाली पेशीय कोशिकाएँ है। ग्लाइकोलिसिस कोशिकाद्रव्य में होती है और लैक्टिक अम्ल ऑक्सीजन की कमी में पेशीय कोशिकाओं में बनता है।
questions.topic: Respiration / Anaerobic respiration / Glycolysis

questions.text:
दर्पण 'X' सूर्य के प्रकाश को सौर भट्टी में सांद्रित करता है तथा दर्पण 'Y' वाहनों के पार्श्व में ड्राइवरों को पीछे के ट्रैफिक को देखने के लिए लगाया जाता है। इन दो दर्पणों के विषय में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से कथन सही हैं?
(i) दर्पण 'X' द्वारा बना प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक, छोटा और इसके फोकस पर होता है।
(ii) दर्पण 'Y' द्वारा बना प्रतिबिम्ब आभासी, छोटा और सीधा होता है।
(iii) दर्पण 'X' द्वारा बना प्रतिबिम्ब आभासी, छोटा और सीधा होता है।
(iv) दर्पण 'Y' द्वारा बना प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक, छोटा और इसके फोकस पर होता है।
questions.text_english:
Mirror 'X' is used to concentrate sunlight in solar furnace and Mirror 'Y' is fitted on the side of the vehicle to see the traffic behind the driver. Which of the following statements are true for the two mirrors?
(i) The image formed by mirror 'X' is real, diminished and at its focus.
(ii) The image formed by mirror 'Y' is virtual, diminished and erect.
(iii) The image formed by mirror 'X' is virtual, diminished and erect.
(iv) The image formed by mirror 'Y' is real, diminished and at its focus.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (i) and (ii). Mirror X is a concave mirror used in a solar furnace to concentrate sunlight at its focus; when the object (sun) is at infinity, the image formed by a concave mirror is real, highly diminished, and located at the focus — so statement (i) is correct. Mirror Y is a convex mirror used as a rear-view mirror; a convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image regardless of object position — so statement (ii) is correct. Statements (iii) and (iv) are incorrect descriptions for the respective mirrors.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) (i) और (ii) है। X अवतल दर्पण है जो वास्तविक, छोटा और फोकस पर प्रतिबिम्ब बनाता है। Y उत्तल दर्पण है जो आभासी, सीधा और छोटा प्रतिबिम्ब बनाता है।
questions.topic: Concave and convex mirrors / Image formation

questions.text: कोई वृद्ध व्यक्ति पक्ष्माभि पेशियों की दुर्बलता तथा अभिनेत्र लेंस के लचीलेपन में कमी होने के कारण दृष्टि दोष से पीड़ित है। यदि यह दृष्टि दोष 'a' है जिसका संशोधन लेंस 'b' द्वारा किया जा सकता है, तो 'a' और 'b' क्रमशः हैं:
questions.text_english: An old person is suffering from an eye defect caused by weakening of ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens. If the defect of vision is 'a' which can be corrected by lens 'b', then 'a' and 'b' respectively are:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) presbyopia and bifocal lens. Presbyopia is an age-related condition caused by gradual weakening of ciliary muscles and loss of flexibility of the eye lens, making it difficult to focus on nearby objects. It is corrected using bifocal lenses, which have a concave upper portion (for distant vision) and a convex lower portion (for near vision). Hypermetropia is a defect of the eye lens shape (not age-related weakening) and is corrected by a convex lens alone. Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected by concave lenses.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) जरा-दूरदृष्टिता और द्विफोकसी लेंस है। वृद्धावस्था में पक्ष्माभि पेशियों के कमजोर होने से जरा-दूरदृष्टिता होती है और इसे द्विफोकसी लेंस से ठीक किया जाता है।
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.topic: Defects of vision / Presbyopia / Bifocal lens

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-कौन से समूह कोई आहार श्रृंखला नहीं बनाते हैं?
(i) लेड़ी, खरगोश, घास, शेर
(ii) प्लवक, मानव, टिड्डा, मछली
(iii) बाज़, घास, सर्प, टिड्डा, मेंढक

questions.text_english:
Which of the following groups do not constitute a food chain?
(i) Wolf, rabbit, grass, lion
(ii) Plankton, man, grasshopper, fish
(iii) Hawk, grass, snake, grasshopper, frog
(iv) Grass, snake, wolf, tiger
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) (ii) and (iv). A valid food chain must begin with a producer (plant) and each organism must eat the one before it in sequence. Group (ii) — Plankton → Grasshopper → Fish → Man: grasshoppers do not eat plankton, so this is not a valid chain. Group (iv) — Grass → Snake → Wolf → Tiger: snakes do not eat grass directly and wolves do not normally eat snakes, so this sequence is incorrect. Group (i) — Grass → Rabbit → Wolf → Lion is a valid chain. Group (iii) — Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk is a valid chain (listed in reverse in the question).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) (ii) और (iv) है। ये दोनों समूह सही क्रम में आहार श्रृंखला नहीं बनाते।

questions.text: किसी स्थलीय पारितंत्र में हरे पादपों की पत्तियों द्वारा प्राप्त सौर ऊर्जा का लगभग कितने प्रतिशत भाग खाद्य ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित नहीं होता है?
questions.text_english: The percentage of solar energy which is not converted into food energy by the leaves of green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 99%. Green plants (producers) capture solar energy through photosynthesis, but only about 1% of the total solar energy incident on leaves is actually converted into chemical (food) energy stored in plant biomass. The remaining 99% is lost — reflected, transmitted, or used for transpiration and other non-photosynthetic processes. This low efficiency of energy capture at the producer level is a fundamental concept in energy flow through ecosystems.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 99% है। हरे पादप सौर ऊर्जा का केवल लगभग 1% भाग ही खाद्य ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित करते हैं। शेष 99% ऊर्जा अन्य प्रक्रियाओं में व्यय हो जाती है।

sub_questions.solution: Besides minimising blood loss, it is essential to plug any leak in a blood vessel to prevent microorganisms (pathogens) from entering the bloodstream through the wound, which could cause infection. The component of blood responsible for this is platelets (thrombocytes). When a blood vessel is damaged, platelets accumulate at the site of injury and release clotting factors. These factors initiate a cascade that converts fibrinogen into fibrin, forming a mesh-like clot that seals the wound and prevents both blood loss and entry of germs.

u = -60 cm, f = -30 cm (concave lens)
v = -20 cm (image is virtual, on the same side as object, 20 cm from lens)

questions.solution: Given: object distance u = -60 cm (sign convention), focal length f = -30 cm (concave lens). Using the lens formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f. Substituting: 1/v - 1/(-60) = 1/(-30), so 1/v + 1/60 = -1/30, therefore 1/v = -1/30 - 1/60 = -2/60 - 1/60 = -3/60 = -1/20. Hence v = -20 cm. The negative sign indicates the image is formed on the same side as the object (virtual image), at a distance of 20 cm from the lens.

Power consumed is 1 watt when 1 joule of electrical energy is consumed per second (i.e., when a current of 1 ampere flows through a potential difference of 1 volt).

questions.text_english: ''Excessive use of chemicals and pesticides in agriculture adversely effect the environment.'' Justify this statement.

key_points: Pesticides and chemicals enter the soil and water bodies, causing pollution and reducing soil fertility.
These chemicals accumulate in organisms through food chains (biological magnification), reaching harmful concentrations in top predators.
Beneficial organisms like bees, earthworms, and soil bacteria are killed, disrupting the ecosystem.

questions.solution: Excessive use of chemicals and pesticides in agriculture harms the environment in multiple ways. Pesticides leach into soil and water bodies, contaminating groundwater and reducing soil fertility. Through the food chain, these chemicals undergo biological magnification — their concentration increases at each trophic level, reaching harmful levels in top predators including humans. Additionally, beneficial organisms such as earthworms, bees, and nitrogen-fixing bacteria are killed, disturbing the ecological balance and reducing biodiversity.

questions.text_english:

(b) Why can metals high up in the reactivity series not be obtained by reduction of their oxides by carbon?

key_points: Example 1: Iron is displaced from copper sulphate solution by more reactive zinc — but in metallurgy, thermite reaction: Fe2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Fe (aluminium displaces iron).
Example 2: Copper is extracted by displacement: CuSO4 + Fe → FeSO4 + Cu (iron displaces copper from its salt solution).
Metals at the top of the reactivity series (Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) are more reactive than carbon and cannot be reduced by carbon; they require electrolytic reduction.

questions.solution: Displacement reactions are used to extract metals in the middle of the reactivity series. For example: (1) The thermite reaction — iron oxide is reduced by aluminium: Fe2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Fe. Here, more reactive aluminium displaces iron. (2) Copper can be extracted from its salt solution by iron: CuSO4 + Fe → FeSO4 + Cu, as iron is more reactive than copper. Metals at the top of the reactivity series (such as sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium) are more reactive than carbon itself. Carbon cannot reduce their oxides because these metals have a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon does. Therefore, electrolytic reduction is used to extract them.

sub_questions.solution: Activity: Take three test tubes. Place an iron nail in the first test tube with plain water (both air and water present). In the second, place a nail in boiled water sealed with oil (no oxygen). In the third, place a nail with anhydrous CaCl2 (no moisture). After a few days, the nail in the first test tube rusts while the nails in the second and third do not. This shows that both water and oxygen are essential for rusting. The chemical reaction is: 4Fe + 3O2 + xH2O → 2Fe2O3·xH2O. This reddish-brown substance is called rust (hydrated iron oxide).

(ग) उपर्युक्त उल्लिखित गति और मटर के पौधे के प्रतानों की गति के बीच अन्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Plants have neither a nervous system nor muscles, even then they respond to stimuli. For example, the leaves of chhui-mui (touch-me-not) plant when touched begin to fold up and droop.
(a) How is the information communicated in 'touch-me-not' plants?
(b) What enables the plant cells to bring out the observable response?
(c) Differentiate the movement mentioned above from the movement of tendrils in a pea plant.

key_points: Information in touch-me-not is transmitted by changes in cell water (turgor pressure) — electrical-chemical signals pass from cell to cell rapidly through the plant.
Change in the amount of water in cells (turgor pressure change) enables observable response — cells lose water and shrink, causing the leaf to droop.
Touch-me-not movement is a nastic movement (not directional, triggered by touch); tendril movement is a tropic movement (directional — thigmotropism — in response to a solid support).

questions.solution: In touch-me-not (Mimosa pudica), information is transmitted through changes in turgor pressure: a touch stimulus triggers electrical-chemical signals that pass rapidly from cell to cell, causing water to leave the cells at the base of leaflets. This change in water content (turgor pressure) causes the cells to shrink, making the leaves fold and droop. The observable response is brought about by the change in turgor of cells. The touch-me-not movement is a nastic (non-directional) movement — it occurs in response to touch regardless of direction. In contrast, the tendril movement of a pea plant is thigmotropism — a directional tropic movement in response to contact with a solid support, driven by differential growth caused by auxin distribution.

questions.text:
(क) गुणसूत्र क्या होते हैं?
(ख) व्याख्या कीजिए कि लैंगिक जनन करने वाले जीवों की स्पीशीज़ में DNA की मात्रा का स्थायित्व किस प्रकार सुनिश्चित होता है।
questions.text_english:
(a) What are chromosomes?
(b) Explain in brief how stability of DNA content of a species is ensured in sexually reproducing organisms?

key_points: Chromosomes are thread-like structures found in the nucleus of cells, made of DNA and proteins (histones). They carry genes that determine hereditary characteristics.

In sexually reproducing organisms, the body (somatic) cells are diploid (2n) — they have two sets of chromosomes. During gamete formation (meiosis), the chromosome number is halved to form haploid (n) gametes.
When two haploid gametes (egg and sperm) fuse during fertilisation, the diploid number (2n) is restored in the zygote. This ensures the DNA content remains constant across generations.

questions.solution: Chromosomes are thread-like structures present in the nucleus of every cell, composed of DNA and proteins. They carry genes that control the inherited characteristics of an organism. In sexually reproducing organisms, the constancy of DNA is maintained through two complementary processes. During gamete formation (meiosis), chromosome number is halved — producing haploid gametes with half the DNA content (n). During fertilisation, a male gamete (n) fuses with a female gamete (n) to form a zygote (2n). This restores the original diploid chromosome number and DNA content, ensuring that each new organism of the species has the same amount of DNA as its parents.
questions.solution_hindi: (क) गुणसूत्र धागेनुमा संरचनाएँ हैं जो केंद्रक में DNA और प्रोटीन से बनी होती हैं और आनुवंशिक लक्षण नियंत्रित करती हैं। (ख) अर्धसूत्री विभाजन से अगुणित (n) युग्मक बनते हैं, निषेचन पर 2n पुनः प्राप्त होता है, जिससे DNA की मात्रा स्थिर रहती है।

questions.text: किसी उत्तल दर्पण द्वारा बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति, स्थिति और सापेक्ष साइज़ को दर्शाने के लिए उस प्रकरण में किरण आरेख खींचिए जिसमें बिम्ब (i) अनन्त पर स्थित है तथा (ii) दर्पण के ध्रुव P और अनन्त के बीच स्थित है।
questions.text_english: Draw ray diagrams to show the nature, position and relative size of the image formed by a convex mirror when the object is placed (i) at infinity and (ii) between infinity and pole P of the mirror.

key_points: Case (i): Object at infinity — incident rays are parallel; reflected rays diverge and appear to come from focus F behind the mirror. Image: at focus F, virtual, erect, highly diminished (point-sized).
Case (ii): Object between infinity and pole P — any position in front of the mirror. Image: between F and P behind the mirror, virtual, erect, and diminished.

Both ray diagrams must show: principal axis, pole P, focus F, centre of curvature C (all behind mirror for convex), two standard rays (one parallel to axis reflected through F, one directed towards F emerging parallel), and the virtual image formed by extending reflected rays behind mirror.

questions.solution: For a convex mirror, the centre of curvature (C) and focus (F) lie behind the reflecting surface. Case (i) — Object at infinity: Parallel rays from an infinitely distant object fall on the convex mirror. The reflected rays diverge and, when extended behind the mirror, appear to meet at the principal focus F. The image is formed at F, is virtual, erect, and highly diminished (point-sized). Case (ii) — Object between infinity and pole P: Two rays are drawn — one parallel to the principal axis (reflected as if coming from F) and one directed towards the centre of curvature (reflected back along the same path). The reflected rays diverge; extending them behind the mirror gives a virtual, erect, and diminished image located between F and P. In both cases the image is virtual, erect, and smaller than the object.
questions.solution_hindi: उत्तल दर्पण के लिए: (i) अनन्त पर बिम्ब — प्रतिबिम्ब फोकस F पर, आभासी, सीधा, बिंदुआकार। (ii) P और अनन्त के बीच बिम्ब — प्रतिबिम्ब F और P के बीच, आभासी, सीधा, छोटा।

Consider the following electric circuit:

(b) The total current drawn from the source
(c) Potential difference across the parallel combination of 10 Ω and 15 Ω resistors

key_points: Parallel combination of 10 Ω and 15 Ω: 1/Rp = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30, so Rp = 6 Ω.

Series combination of 60 Ω and 40 Ω: Rs = 60 + 40 = 100 Ω. Wait — from circuit diagram: 10 Ω and 15 Ω are in parallel (= 6 Ω), and 60 Ω and 40 Ω are in series (= 100 Ω). But circuit shows 60 Ω and 40 Ω in parallel with each other? Re-examining: the circuit shows 10 Ω || 15 Ω in one branch and 60 Ω and 40 Ω in series in another branch, all connected to 15 V. Total: Rp(10,15) = 6 Ω; R(60+40) = 100 Ω; but from diagram, the 60 Ω and 40 Ω are in series with each other and this series combination is in parallel with the (10+15) parallel set? Actually from diagram, the parallel combination of 10 and 15 is in series with the series combination of 60 and 40. Total R = 6 + 60 + 40 = 106 Ω? Let me re-read: circuit has battery 15V, switch K, 60 Ω and 40 Ω in series at bottom, and 10 Ω parallel with 15 Ω at the top. All in one loop means: R_total = Rp(10,15) + 60 + 40 = 6 + 100 = 106 Ω. I = V/R = 15/106 ≈ 0.14 A. V across parallel = I × Rp = (15/106) × 6 = 90/106 ≈ 0.85 V.

An ammeter A is shown in the circuit. The parallel combination (10 Ω || 15 Ω) is connected in series with the 60 Ω and 40 Ω resistors.

This parallel combination is in series with 60 Ω and 40 Ω. (a) Total resistance = 6 + 60 + 40 = 106 Ω. (b) Total current I = V/R = 15/106 ≈ 0.14 A (or 15/106 A). (c) Potential difference across the parallel combination = I × Rp = (15/106) × 6 = 90/106 = 45/53 ≈ 0.85 V.

questions.text_english:
(a) Write the relationship between resistivity and resistance of a cylindrical conductor of length l and area of cross-section A. Hence derive the SI unit of resistivity.
(b) Why are alloys used in electrical heating devices?

key_points: R = ρl/A, where ρ is resistivity. So ρ = RA/l.
SI unit of ρ: [ρ] = [R][A]/[l] = Ω × m² / m = Ω·m (ohm-metre).
Alloys are used in heating devices because they have high resistivity, high melting points, and do not oxidise (burn) easily at high temperatures.

questions.solution: The resistance R of a cylindrical conductor is related to its resistivity ρ, length l, and cross-sectional area A by: R = ρl/A. Rearranging: ρ = RA/l. The SI unit of resistivity is derived as: [ρ] = [R] × [A] / [l] = Ω × m² / m = Ω·m (ohm-metre). Alloys are preferred in electrical heating devices (such as electric irons and geysers) for three reasons: they have much higher resistivity than pure metals, allowing generation of more heat; they have very high melting points, so they do not melt at high operating temperatures; and they do not oxidise (or burn) readily even at high temperatures, making them durable.

key_points: But-1-ene: CH2=CH-CH2-CH3 (double bond between C1 and C2)
But-2-ene: CH3-CH=CH-CH3 (double bond between C2 and C3)

sub_questions.solution: Two isomers of Butene (C4H8) are: (1) But-1-ene: CH2=CH-CH2-CH3 — the double bond is between the first and second carbon atoms. (2) But-2-ene: CH3-CH=CH-CH3 — the double bond is between the second and third carbon atoms. Both have the molecular formula C4H8 but differ in the position of the double bond.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों के नाम लिखिए: (I) 3-कार्बन श्रृंखला + Cl अंत में (II) बीच में C=O समूह (बुटेनोन)
sub_questions.text_english: Name the following compounds: (I) 3-carbon chain with Cl at end (II) Compound with C=O in middle (butanone)

key_points: (I) 1-chloropropane (or chloropropane) — CH3-CH2-CH2-Cl
(II) Butanone (or methyl ethyl ketone) — CH3-CO-CH2-CH3

sub_questions.solution: Compound (I) shows a 3-carbon chain with a chlorine atom at the terminal carbon: CH3-CH2-CH2-Cl. Its IUPAC name is 1-chloropropane. Compound (II) shows a 4-carbon chain with a carbonyl group (C=O) at the second carbon position (a ketone): CH3-CO-CH2-CH3. Its IUPAC name is butanone (also called methyl ethyl ketone).

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं के रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए तथा प्रत्येक के लिए आवश्यक एक शर्त का उल्लेख कीजिए: (I) एथेनॉल का पूर्ण ऑक्सीकरण (II) प्रोपीन का हाइड्रोजनीकरण (III) एथेनॉइक अम्ल की एथेनॉल से अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Write chemical equations for: (I) Complete oxidation of ethanol (II) Hydrogenation of propene (III) Reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol

key_points: (I) C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O; Condition: burning/combustion (presence of oxygen/air and ignition)
(II) CH3-CH=CH2 + H2 → CH3-CH2-CH3; Condition: nickel (Ni) catalyst and heat
(III) CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O; Condition: concentrated H2SO4 as catalyst and gentle heating (esterification)

sub_questions.solution: Reactions with conditions: (I) Complete oxidation (combustion) of ethanol: C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O. Condition: presence of excess oxygen (air) and ignition. (II) Hydrogenation of propene: CH3CH=CH2 + H2 → CH3CH2CH3 (propane). Condition: nickel (Ni) catalyst and heat. (III) Esterification — ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol: CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (ethyl ethanoate + water). Condition: a few drops of concentrated H2SO4 as catalyst and gentle heating.

sub_questions.text: कोई कार्बन यौगिक X अच्छा विलायक है। सोडियम से अभिक्रिया करके, X दो उत्पाद Y और Z बनाता है। Z का उपयोग वनस्पति तेल को वनस्पति घी में परिवर्तित करने में किया जाता है। X, Y और Z को पहचानिए और इनके नाम लिखिए। X की सोडियम से अभिक्रिया का समीकरण भी लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: A carbon compound X is a good solvent. On reaction with sodium, X forms two products Y and Z. Z is used to convert vegetable oil into vegetable ghee. Identify and name X, Y and Z. Also write the equation of reaction of X with sodium.

key_points: X is ethanol (C2H5OH) — a good solvent.
Y is sodium ethoxide (C2H5ONa).
Z is hydrogen gas (H2) — used in hydrogenation of vegetable oil to make vegetable ghee.
Equation: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2↑

sub_questions.solution: X is ethanol (C2H5OH) — it is a good solvent used in medicines, perfumes, and paints. When ethanol reacts with sodium metal, it produces sodium ethoxide (Y = C2H5ONa) and hydrogen gas (Z = H2). Hydrogen gas is used for the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to convert them into vegetable ghee (a solid fat). The equation is: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2↑. This confirms that X is ethanol, Y is sodium ethoxide, and Z is hydrogen gas.

sub_questions.text: यह दर्शाने के लिए रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए कि क्या होता है जब: (I) एथेनॉल का ऑक्सीजन/वायु में दहन होता है। (II) एथेनॉल को 443 K पर आधिक्य सांद्र H2SO4 के साथ गर्म किया जाता है। (III) एथेनॉल अम्लीकृत पोटैशियम डाइक्रोमेट के साथ अभिक्रिया करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Write chemical equation to show what happens when ethanol: (I) burns in oxygen/air. (II) is heated at 443 K in excess conc. H2SO4. (III) reacts with acidified potassium dichromate.

key_points: (I) C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O (combustion)
(II) C2H5OH (excess H2SO4, 443K) → CH2=CH2 + H2O (dehydration to ethene)
(III) C2H5OH + [O] (K2Cr2O7/H2SO4) → CH3CHO → CH3COOH (oxidation: ethanol → ethanal → ethanoic acid)

sub_questions.solution: Three reactions of ethanol: (I) Combustion in air: C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O. Ethanol burns with a blue flame producing carbon dioxide and water. (II) Dehydration with excess conc. H2SO4 at 443 K: C2H5OH → CH2=CH2 + H2O. Ethanol loses a water molecule to form ethene (an alkene). (III) Oxidation with acidified K2Cr2O7: C2H5OH + [O] → CH3CHO (ethanal) and further oxidation gives CH3COOH (ethanoic acid). The orange dichromate turns green as it oxidises ethanol.

(I) अण्डाशय
(II) अंडवाहिका (फेलोपियन ट्यूब)
(III) गर्भाशय
(ii) पुरुषों (मानव नरों) द्वारा उपयोग की जाने वाली दो गर्भनिरोधक विधियों का संक्षेप में उल्लेख कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Write the functions of the following parts of human female reproductive system:
(I) Ovary
(II) Fallopian tube
(III) Uterus
(ii) State briefly two contraceptive methods used by human males.
OR
(b) (i) Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
(ii) Identify A, B and C in the diagram given below and write one function of each.

sub_questions.text: अण्डाशय का कार्य
sub_questions.text_english: Function of Ovary

key_points: The ovary produces female gametes (eggs/ova) and secretes female sex hormones — oestrogen and progesterone.

sub_questions.solution: The ovary produces female gametes called ova (eggs) through a process called oogenesis. It also secretes female sex hormones — oestrogen and progesterone — which regulate the menstrual cycle and the development of secondary sexual characteristics.

sub_questions.text: अंडवाहिका (फेलोपियन ट्यूब) का कार्य
sub_questions.text_english: Function of Fallopian tube

key_points: The fallopian tube transports the egg from the ovary to the uterus; it is also the site of fertilisation.

sub_questions.solution: The fallopian tube (oviduct) conducts the mature egg (ovum) released from the ovary towards the uterus. It is also the site where fertilisation of the egg by a sperm typically takes place. Cilia lining the tube help move the egg or fertilised zygote towards the uterus.

sub_questions.text: गर्भाशय का कार्य
sub_questions.text_english: Function of Uterus

key_points: The uterus receives and nourishes the fertilised egg (zygote); it is where the embryo implants and develops into a foetus during pregnancy.

sub_questions.solution: The uterus (womb) is the site of implantation of the fertilised egg. It provides nourishment and protection to the developing embryo and foetus throughout pregnancy. The uterine wall (endometrium) thickens each month to receive a fertilised egg; if fertilisation does not occur, the endometrium sheds during menstruation.

sub_questions.text: पुरुषों द्वारा उपयोग की जाने वाली दो गर्भनिरोधक विधियाँ
sub_questions.text_english: Two contraceptive methods used by human males

key_points: Condom: A physical barrier device worn over the penis during intercourse to prevent sperm from entering the female reproductive tract.
Vasectomy: A surgical procedure in which the vas deferens is cut and tied to permanently prevent sperm from being released during ejaculation.

sub_questions.solution: Two contraceptive methods used by human males are: (1) Condom — a thin sheath made of latex that is worn over the penis during sexual intercourse to act as a physical barrier, preventing sperm from entering the female reproductive tract. It also protects against sexually transmitted infections. (2) Vasectomy — a permanent surgical method in which the vas deferens (sperm-carrying duct) is cut and tied (ligated), preventing sperm from being released during ejaculation.

sub_questions.text: स्वपरागण और परपरागण के बीच विभेदन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination.

key_points: Self-pollination: transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of the same flower or another flower on the same plant. Requires only one plant. Does not increase genetic variation.
Cross-pollination: transfer of pollen from the anther of one flower to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species. Requires two plants. Increases genetic diversity in offspring.

sub_questions.solution: Self-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower, or to another flower on the same plant. It requires only one plant and does not introduce genetic variation in the offspring. In contrast, cross-pollination involves transfer of pollen from the anther of one plant to the stigma of another plant of the same species, facilitated by agents like wind, insects, or water. Cross-pollination requires two plants and introduces genetic diversity in the offspring.

sub_questions.text: नीचे दिए गए आरेख में A, B और C की पहचान कीजिए और प्रत्येक भाग का एक कार्य लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify A, B and C in the diagram given below and write one function of each.

key_points: A = Stigma: receives pollen grains during pollination.
B = Style: connects stigma to the ovary; provides a pathway for the pollen tube to grow towards the ovule.
C = Ovary: contains ovules; after fertilisation, it develops into the fruit, and ovules develop into seeds.

sub_questions.solution: From the diagram of a pistil (female reproductive part of a flower): A is the Stigma — it is the sticky top part of the pistil that receives pollen grains during pollination. B is the Style — it is the stalk-like middle part connecting the stigma to the ovary; it provides a pathway for the pollen tube to grow down towards the ovule. C is the Ovary — it is the swollen basal part containing ovules; after fertilisation, the ovary develops into the fruit while the ovules become seeds.

questions.text:
(क) (i) किसी लेंस 'X' की क्षमता – 2·5 D है। इस लेंस का नाम लिखिए और इसकी फोकस दूरी cm में निर्धारित कीजिए। नेत्र चिकित्सक किस दृष्टि दोष के संशोधन के लिए इस प्रकार के लेंस को संशोधक लेंस के रूप में निर्धारित करते हैं?
(ii) ''किसी लेंस के लिए आवर्धन 'm' का मान – 2 है।'' नई कार्तीय चिह्न परिपाटी का उपयोग करते हुए और यह मानते हुए कि कोई बिम्ब इस लेंस के प्रकाशिक केन्द्र से 20 cm की दूरी पर है, निम्नलिखित का उल्लेख कीजिए:
(I) बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति;
(II) बिम्ब के साइज़ की तुलना में प्रतिबिम्ब का साइज़;
(III) प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति, तथा
(IV) प्रतिबिम्ब की ऊँचाई का चिह्न।
(iii) दो लेंसों A और B की फोकस दूरी के संख्यात्मक मान क्रमशः 10 cm और 20 cm हैं। इन दोनों में से कौन-सा लेंस अभिसारिता/अपसारिता की उच्चतर कोटि दर्शाएगा? अपने उत्तर की कारण सहित पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a)(i) The power of a lens 'X' is -2.5 D. Name the lens and determine its focal length in cm. For which eye defect of vision will an optician prescribe this type of lens as a corrective lens?
(ii) The value of magnification 'm' for a lens is -2. Using new Cartesian Sign Convention and considering that an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, state: (I) the nature of the image formed; (II) size of the image compared to the size of the object; (III) position of the image, and (IV) sign of the height of the image.
(iii) The numerical values of the focal lengths of two lenses A and B are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively. Which one of the two will show higher degree of convergence/divergence? Give reason to justify your answer.
OR
(b)(i) Draw a ray diagram to show the refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab when it falls obliquely from air into glass.
(ii) State Snell's law of refraction of light.
(iii) Differentiate between the virtual images formed by a convex lens and a concave lens on the basis of: (I) object distance, and (II) magnification.

sub_questions.text: लेंस X की क्षमता –2.5 D है। इसका नाम और फोकस दूरी तथा किस दृष्टि दोष में उपयोग।
sub_questions.text_english: Power of lens X is -2.5 D. Name it, find focal length in cm, and identify the eye defect corrected.

key_points: Negative power → concave (diverging) lens.
Used for myopia (short-sightedness / near-sightedness).

sub_questions.solution: Since the power of lens X is negative (-2.5 D), it is a concave (diverging) lens. The focal length is calculated as: f = 1/P = 1/(-2.5) = -0.4 m = -40 cm. A concave lens is prescribed by opticians to correct myopia (short-sightedness), a defect in which the image of distant objects is formed in front of the retina rather than on it. The concave lens diverges the incoming rays, shifting the image back onto the retina.

sub_questions.text: आवर्धन m = -2, बिम्ब दूरी 20 cm: (I) प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति (II) साइज़ (III) स्थिति (IV) ऊँचाई का चिह्न
sub_questions.text_english: Magnification m = -2, object at 20 cm. State: (I) nature, (II) size, (III) position, (IV) sign of height of image.

key_points: (I) Real and inverted (m is negative → real and inverted image for a lens).
(II) Image is twice the size of the object (|m| = 2, so image height = 2 × object height).
(III) Position: m = v/u; u = -20 cm; m = -2; so v = m × u = (-2) × (-20) = +40 cm. Image is 40 cm on the other side of the lens.
(IV) Sign of image height is negative (inverted image, below principal axis).

sub_questions.solution: Given m = -2 and object distance u = -20 cm (using sign convention). (I) Nature: since m is negative, the image is real and inverted. (II) Size: |m| = 2, so the image is twice the size of the object (magnified). (III) Position: using m = v/u, we get v = m × u = (-2) × (-20) = +40 cm. The image is formed 40 cm on the opposite side of the lens (positive sign means beyond the lens). (IV) The height of the image is negative (the image is inverted, i.e., below the principal axis).

sub_questions.text: दो लेंसों A (f = 10 cm) और B (f = 20 cm) में से कौन अभिसारिता/अपसारिता की उच्चतर कोटि दर्शाएगा?
sub_questions.text_english: Lenses A (f = 10 cm) and B (f = 20 cm). Which shows higher convergence/divergence and why?

key_points: Lens A (f = 10 cm) shows higher degree of convergence or divergence.
Power = 1/f; PA = 1/0.10 = 10 D; PB = 1/0.20 = 5 D. Higher power = shorter focal length = greater ability to converge/diverge light.

sub_questions.solution: Lens A with focal length 10 cm shows a higher degree of convergence (if convex) or divergence (if concave). This is because the power of a lens is inversely proportional to its focal length: P = 1/f. Power of A = 1/0.10 = 10 D; Power of B = 1/0.20 = 5 D. Since Lens A has greater power (10 D > 5 D), it bends light rays more strongly, exhibiting a higher degree of convergence or divergence compared to Lens B.

sub_questions.text: काँच के आयताकार स्लैब से प्रकाश की किरण का अपवर्तन दर्शाने के लिए किरण आरेख खींचिए जबकि प्रकाश किरण वायु से काँच में तिरछी आपतन कर रही है।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw a ray diagram to show the refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab when it falls obliquely from air into glass.

key_points: Incident ray in air bends towards the normal at the first surface (air to glass, denser medium).
Refracted ray inside glass travels at a smaller angle to normal.
At the second surface (glass to air), the ray bends away from normal and the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally displaced.

sub_questions.solution: The ray diagram should show: an incident ray in air hitting the first surface of the glass slab obliquely. At this interface, the ray bends towards the normal (since glass is optically denser than air) — this is the refracted ray inside the glass. When this ray hits the second surface, it bends away from the normal (going from glass back to air). The final emergent ray is parallel to the original incident ray but shifted sideways — this lateral shift is called lateral displacement. The normal at both surfaces, angle of incidence (i), angle of refraction (r), and lateral displacement should all be labelled.

sub_questions.text: प्रकाश के अपवर्तन का स्नेल का नियम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State Snell's law of refraction of light.

key_points: The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media: sin i / sin r = constant (= n, the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first).
Also: the incident ray, the refracted ray, and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.

sub_questions.solution: Snell's law of refraction states: (1) The incident ray, the refracted ray, and the normal to the interface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane. (2) The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (i) to the sine of the angle of refraction (r) is a constant for a given pair of media. Mathematically: sin i / sin r = n21 (the refractive index of medium 2 with respect to medium 1). This constant is also equal to the ratio of the speed of light in medium 1 to the speed of light in medium 2.

sub_questions.text: उत्तल लेंस और अवतल लेंस द्वारा बने आभासी प्रतिबिम्बों के बीच (I) बिम्ब दूरी तथा (II) आवर्धन के आधार पर विभेदन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between the virtual images formed by a convex lens and a concave lens on the basis of: (I) object distance, and (II) magnification.

key_points: (I) Object distance: Convex lens forms a virtual image only when the object is placed between F and optical centre (u < f). Concave lens always forms a virtual image regardless of object position.
(II) Magnification: Convex lens gives m > 1 (magnified virtual image). Concave lens gives 0 < m < 1 (diminished virtual image, always smaller than object).

sub_questions.solution: A convex lens forms a virtual image only when the object is placed between the optical centre and the principal focus (object distance < focal length). In this case, the magnification is greater than 1 (m > 1), meaning the virtual image is magnified (larger than the object) and erect. A concave lens, on the other hand, always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image regardless of the object's position. Its magnification is always positive but less than 1 (0 < m < 1), meaning the image is always smaller than the object.

questions.text: समुद्री जल में कई प्रकार के लवण घुले होते हैं। साधारण नमक को इन लवणों से पृथक किया जाता है। विश्व के कई भागों में ठोस लवण का निक्षेप होता है। बड़े आकार के यह क्रिस्टल प्रायः अपद्रव्यों (अशुद्धियों) के कारण भूरे रंग के होते हैं। इसे खनिज नमक कहते हैं। इसका खनन भी कोयले की भाँति होता है। साधारण नमक दैनिक जीवन में उपयोग होने वाले रसायनों के लिए एक महत्त्वपूर्ण कच्ची सामग्री है।
questions.text_english: Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use.

sub_questions.text: (क) लवण-जल (ब्राइन) के विद्युत-अपघटन से उत्पन्न उत्पादों को दर्शाने के लिए संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write balanced chemical equations to show the products formed during electrolysis of brine.

key_points: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl2(g) + H2(g)
Products: sodium hydroxide (NaOH), chlorine gas (Cl2), and hydrogen gas (H2).

sub_questions.solution: The electrolysis of brine (concentrated aqueous sodium chloride solution) is represented by: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl2(g) + H2(g). At the cathode, hydrogen gas is produced (H2); at the anode, chlorine gas is liberated (Cl2); and sodium hydroxide solution (NaOH) remains in the solution. This process is also called the chlor-alkali process.

sub_questions.text: (ख) लवण-जल (ब्राइन) के विद्युत-अपघटन से प्राप्त किसी भी एक उत्पाद के दो उपयोगों की सूची बनाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: List two uses of any one product obtained during electrolysis of brine.

key_points: NaOH: used in making soap and detergents; used in paper manufacturing (pulp industry).
OR Cl2: used for disinfecting drinking water; used in manufacturing PVC and bleaching powder.
OR H2: used as fuel (hydrogen fuel cells); used in hydrogenation of vegetable oils.

sub_questions.solution: Two uses of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) obtained from brine electrolysis: (1) It is used in making soaps and detergents — fats and oils are treated with NaOH in a process called saponification. (2) It is used in the paper industry to dissolve lignin from wood pulp during paper manufacturing. (Alternatively, chlorine is used to disinfect water supplies and to manufacture PVC plastic and bleaching powder; hydrogen is used as rocket fuel and in hydrogenation of oils.)

sub_questions.text: (ग)(i) किसी दुर्बल असंक्षारक क्षारीय लवण 'A' का उपयोग खाने को शीघ्रता से पकाने में किया जाता है। इसे गर्म करने पर कोई यौगिक 'B' बनता है जिसका उपयोग जल की स्थायी कठोरता को दूर करने में किया जाता है। A और B को पहचानिए तथा A को गर्म करने पर होने वाली अभिक्रिया का समीकरण भी लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: A mild non-corrosive basic salt 'A', used for faster cooking, is strongly heated to produce a compound 'B', that is used for removing permanent hardness of water. Identify A and B and also write the equation for the reaction that occurs when A is heated.

key_points: A = Sodium hydrogen carbonate / baking soda (NaHCO3)
B = Sodium carbonate / washing soda (Na2CO3)
2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2 (on heating)

sub_questions.solution: Salt A is sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3), commonly known as baking soda. It is a mild, non-corrosive basic salt used in cooking (in baking powder) to make food rise quickly. On strong heating, it decomposes to give compound B — sodium carbonate (Na2CO3), also known as washing soda. Sodium carbonate is used to remove permanent hardness of water because it precipitates Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions as insoluble carbonates. The equation is: 2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2↑.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(ii) क्रिस्टलन के जल की परिभाषा लिखिए। उन दो लवणों का उदाहरण दीजिए जिनमें क्रिस्टलन का जल होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Define water of crystallisation. Give two examples of salts that have water of crystallisation.

key_points: Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules that are chemically combined with one formula unit of a salt in its crystalline form.
Examples: Copper sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO4·5H2O, blue vitriol) and sodium carbonate decahydrate (Na2CO3·10H2O, washing soda).

sub_questions.solution: Water of crystallisation is defined as the fixed number of water molecules that are chemically bonded and incorporated into the crystal structure of a salt. These water molecules are essential for maintaining the crystalline form; on heating, the salt loses these water molecules and becomes anhydrous. Two examples of salts with water of crystallisation are: (1) Blue vitriol — copper sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO4·5H2O), which is blue in colour. (2) Washing soda — sodium carbonate decahydrate (Na2CO3·10H2O).

questions.text: सभी जीवों का अनुरक्षण कार्यनिरन्तर होना चाहिए। यह उस समय भी चलते रहना चाहिए जब वे कोई विशेष कार्य नहीं कर रहे होते हैं। जब हम सो रहे हों अथवा अपनी कक्षा में बैठे होते हैं, उस समय भी यह अनुरक्षण का काम चलता रहना चाहिए। कोशिकाओं और ऊतकों की क्षति और टूट-फूट को रोकने तथा अनुरक्षण प्रक्रियाओं के लिए ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है। यह ऊर्जा एकल जीव के शरीर को स्वपोषियों, जिन्हें उत्पादक कहते हैं, से प्राप्त होती है।
questions.text_english: The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.
questions.instruction_line: केस को सावधानीपूर्वक पढ़िए और दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the case carefully and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: (क) उस प्रक्रिया का नाम और परिभाषा लिखिए जिसके द्वारा हरे पादप भोजन निर्मित करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Name and define the process by which green plants prepare food.

key_points: Photosynthesis: the process by which green plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to prepare food (glucose) in the presence of chlorophyll.

sub_questions.solution: The process is called photosynthesis. It is defined as the process by which green plants (and some other organisms) use the energy of sunlight, absorbed by the pigment chlorophyll present in chloroplasts, to convert carbon dioxide (from the air) and water (from the soil) into glucose (food/chemical energy) and oxygen as a by-product.

sub_questions.text: (ख) उपर्युक्त प्रक्रिया में होने वाली अभिक्रिया का रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write chemical equation involved in the above process.

key_points: 6CO2 + 6H2O → (sunlight, chlorophyll) → C6H12O6 + 6O2

sub_questions.solution: The overall chemical equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light energy → C6H12O6 + 6O2. This represents six molecules of carbon dioxide reacting with six molecules of water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll to produce one molecule of glucose (C6H12O6) and six molecules of oxygen gas.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(i) मरुद्स्थलीय (मरुस्थली) पौधों द्वारा भोजन के संश्लेषण के समय होने वाली घटनाओं का उचित अनुक्रम में उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State in proper sequence the events that occur in synthesis of food by desert plants.

key_points: 1. Stomata open at night (not during the day) to absorb CO2 and store it as organic acids to prevent water loss.
2. During the day, stomata close; stored CO2 is used during light reactions.
3. Light energy is absorbed by chlorophyll; water molecules are split (photolysis), releasing O2.
4. Carbohydrates (glucose) are synthesised using stored CO2 and hydrogen from water through the Calvin cycle.

sub_questions.solution: Desert plants (CAM plants like cacti) have evolved a special mechanism to conserve water. The sequence of events is: (1) At night, stomata open and CO2 is absorbed and fixed into organic acids (such as malic acid) which are stored in vacuoles. (2) During the day, stomata remain closed to prevent water loss. (3) Stored organic acids release CO2 inside the leaf. (4) Light energy absorbed by chlorophyll splits water (photolysis), releasing O2 and generating ATP and NADPH. (5) The released CO2 is fixed through the Calvin cycle to produce glucose.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(ii) कारण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए कि (I) घटा वाले (मेघाच्छन्न) मौसम में, तथा (II) धूल द्वारा रंध्रों को बंद कर दिए जाने पर हरे पादपों द्वारा भोजन निर्माण करने की दर पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain giving reasons what happens to the rate at which the green plants will prepare food: (I) during cloudy weather, and (II) when stomata get blocked due to dust.

key_points: (I) Cloudy weather: rate of photosynthesis decreases because less sunlight is available; light is a necessary raw material for the light reactions of photosynthesis.
(II) Blocked stomata: rate of photosynthesis decreases because CO2 cannot enter the leaf; CO2 is required as a raw material for the dark reactions (Calvin cycle).

sub_questions.solution: Two conditions and their effects on photosynthesis: (I) During cloudy weather, the rate of photosynthesis decreases significantly because sunlight intensity is reduced. Light is essential for the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis where water is split and ATP/NADPH are produced. Less light means less energy available for glucose synthesis. (II) When stomata are blocked by dust, CO2 cannot enter the leaves from the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide is a raw material for the dark reactions (Calvin cycle) where it is fixed into glucose. With insufficient CO2, the rate of food preparation by green plants will decrease markedly.

questions.text: हम अपने घरों में विद्युत शक्ति की आपूर्ति मुख्य तारों, जिसे मेन्स भी कहते हैं, से प्राप्त करते हैं। ये मुख्य तार या तो धरती पर लगे विद्युत खम्बों के सहारे अथवा भूमिगत केबलों द्वारा हमारे घरों तक पहुँचते हैं। हमारे देश में इस आपूर्ति के दो तारों (विद्युन्मय तार तथा उदासीन तार) के बीच 220 V का विभवान्तर होता है।
questions.text_english: In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V.
questions.instruction_line: केस को सावधानीपूर्वक पढ़िए और दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the case carefully and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: (क) हमारे घरों को आने वाली आपूर्ति जिन लाइन तारों द्वारा होती है उनके विद्युतरोधी आवरणों के रंग लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the colours of the insulation covers of the line wires through which supply comes to our homes.

key_points: Live wire: Red insulation (in older systems) or Brown (in newer systems).
Neutral wire: Black insulation (older) or Blue (newer).
Earth wire: Green insulation.

sub_questions.solution: The domestic supply to our homes uses three wires with different coloured insulation: (1) Live wire (phase wire) — has red insulation (or brown in newer international standards). (2) Neutral wire — has black insulation (or blue in newer standards). (3) Earth wire — has green insulation. The live wire carries current at 220 V; the neutral wire is at zero potential; the earth wire provides a safety path to the ground.

sub_questions.text: (ख) 220 V के किसी विद्युत परिपथ का धारा अनुमतांक क्या होना चाहिए कि उस परिपथ पर 1 kW शक्ति अनुमतांक की विद्युत इस्तरी का प्रचालन किया जा सके?
sub_questions.text_english: What should be the current rating of the electric circuit (220 V) so that an electric iron of 1 kW power rating can be operated?

key_points: I = P/V = 1000/220 = 4.54 A ≈ 4.5 A. The circuit should have a current rating of at least 5 A.

sub_questions.solution: The current required to operate the electric iron is calculated using P = VI, so I = P/V = 1000 W / 220 V = 4.54 A ≈ 4.5 A. Therefore, the circuit must have a current rating of at least 5 A (the next standard fuse or circuit breaker rating above 4.5 A) to safely operate the 1 kW electric iron without tripping the circuit.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(i) भूसम्पर्क तार का क्या कार्य है? विद्युत इस्तरी जैसे घरेलू विद्युत साधित्रों में भूसम्पर्क तार के महत्त्व का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What is the function of the earth wire? State the advantage of the earth wire in domestic electric appliances such as electric iron.

key_points: The earth wire provides a low-resistance path to the ground for any leakage current.

In appliances like an electric iron, if the live wire accidentally touches the metallic body, the leakage current flows safely to the earth through the earth wire instead of through the user's body, preventing electric shock.

sub_questions.solution: The earth wire is a safety wire that provides a low-resistance conducting path directly to the ground (earth). Its main function is to protect users from electric shock. In domestic appliances like an electric iron, the metallic casing is connected to the earth wire. If due to any fault, the live wire comes in contact with the metallic body of the appliance, the leakage current flows to the earth through the earth wire (which has very low resistance) rather than through the user's body. This prevents electric shock and protects both the user and the appliance.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(ii) विद्युत से होने वाली दुर्घटनाओं से बचाव के लिए ली जाने वाली दो सावधानियों की सूची बनाइए। उल्लेख कीजिए कि ये सावधानियाँ किस प्रकार परिपथ/साधित्र को संभावित क्षति से बचाती हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: List two precautions to be taken to avoid electrical accidents. State how these precautions prevent possible damage to the circuit/appliance.

key_points: Precaution 1: Use a fuse or MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) in the circuit. When current exceeds the safe limit, the fuse wire melts (or MCB trips), breaking the circuit and preventing overheating, fire, or damage to appliances.

Precaution 2: Do not use damaged or exposed wires / do not touch electrical appliances with wet hands. This prevents short circuits and reduces the risk of current flowing through the human body, avoiding electric shock.

sub_questions.solution: Two precautions to avoid electrical accidents: (1) Use a fuse or Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB) in every circuit. A fuse contains a thin wire with a low melting point; if the current exceeds the rated limit due to overloading or a short circuit, the fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit, preventing damage to wiring and appliances. (2) Never touch electrical switches or appliances with wet hands, and use insulated tools. Water is a conductor of electricity; touching live wires or appliances with wet hands allows current to flow through the body, causing electric shock. Dry hands and insulated tools prevent this hazard.
